story_type: rocket plane altitude record climb seen from the cockpit, historic color film
hook: The view from a rocket plane at 136,500 feet.
narration: This is the view from a rocket plane climbing to the edge of space.
Air Force Major Bob White was at the controls of the X-15.
He pulled up into a climb so steep it felt almost straight up.
The altimeter wound past one hundred thousand feet and kept going.
[short pause] Then the engine burned out, and the plane coasted higher still.
Up there the air is so thin that ordinary wings and tail fins can barely steer.
White said the dark blue sky and the bright band around the Earth were the most dramatic sight of all.
outcome: White came back down with a new altitude record of 136,500 feet.
preview_ok: Cockpit window shots show the dark sky over the Earth, and the altimeter is a white dial on black; both trip DARK but the subject fills the frame.
title: X-15 climbs to 136,500 feet
question_comment: Would you have taken this ride to the edge of space?

facts.claim: Major Bob White flew a 136,500 foot record altitude flight on Aug. 12
facts.source_quote: Then on the 12th of August, just eight days later, Major Bob White was up before the cameras after his 136,500 foot record breaking altitude flight.

facts.claim: The climb felt almost straight up
facts.source_quote: I was very definitely impressed that I was going, well almost, straight up.

facts.claim: Burnout, then the plane kept climbing
Dark blue sky and the lighter band around the Earth were the most dramatic
facts.source_quote: What you see at this altitude impressed me as being the most dramatic point of flying at over 130,000 feet.

description:
Air Force Maj. Bob White flies the X-15 rocket plane to a record 136,500 feet on Aug. 12, 1960, filmed from the cockpit.
